selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What happens when a person makes this short worldly life his biggest goal?
questions.answer: He lives in a bad state inside, even if life looks nice on the outside.

questions.question: If someone truly turns toward the life that lasts forever, what does he receive?
questions.answer: He gets happiness in this life and in the next life.

questions.question: Which life in the passage is short and does not last?
questions.answer: Life in this world.

questions.question: Which life in the passage lasts forever?
questions.answer: The life to come.

questions.question: How might this world feel for a person who cares about the next life?
questions.answer: It may feel hard and upsetting.

questions.question: Why can that person keep going even when life is hard?
questions.answer: He sees this world as a place to wait before Paradise.

questions.question: What good actions does that person do while facing hardship?
questions.answer: He stays patient and thanks Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage teach us to chase only this world or to care most about the next life?
questions.answer: It teaches us to care most about the next life.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: We should not make this world our main goal; we should aim for the life to come.

questions.question: What kind of life is this world called in the passage?
questions.answer: A life that passes quickly.

questions.question: Can someone look happy on the outside but still be in a very bad condition inside?
questions.answer: Yes. A person may seem to be in a good place but still be miserable inside.

questions.question: Who receives the happiness of both worlds?
questions.answer: The person who sincerely aims for eternal life.

questions.question: What does “both worlds” mean here?
questions.answer: This life and the next life.

questions.question: What picture is used to describe this world for a believer?
questions.answer: A waiting place before Paradise.

questions.question: How should a person act while waiting through the hard parts of life?
questions.answer: With patience and thankfulness.

questions.question: If life is tough, does that mean a person has no happiness at all?
questions.answer: No. A person who aims for the next life can still have real happiness.

questions.question: In the passage, what mistake does a person make if he lives only for this world?
questions.answer: He makes the world his main purpose.

questions.question: What is wrong with making only this world your purpose?
questions.answer: It leads to inner misery, even if things seem pleasant.

questions.question: What kind of turning toward eternal life is mentioned?
questions.answer: A serious and sincere turning.

questions.question: What reward comes from that sincere turning?
questions.answer: Happiness in both lives.

questions.question: According to the passage, can this world still be painful for a good person?
questions.answer: Yes. It can still be difficult and sad.

questions.question: What thought helps that person bear the pain?
questions.answer: Thinking of this world as only a waiting room before Paradise.

questions.question: What two beautiful qualities are named at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Patience and thankfulness.

questions.question: Which person is doing better in the passage: the one who loves only this world, or the one who prepares for the next life?
questions.answer: The one who prepares for the next life.
